title: Hardware-aware baseline sampler and release-blurb presets for micro-changelogs
author: Anika Shah

description: Context: We onboard a growing set of model/hardware pairings (A100, H100, G5, aarch64 inference nodes) and need compact, actionable baselines plus small changelog blurbs to help downstream teams interpret model rollouts. This PR introduces a lightweight hardware-aware baseline sampler that collects a small set of latency and throughput percentiles per hardware class, and a release-blurb preset registry that can generate concise micro-changelogs for model version releases. Motivation: Current model profiles produce large, noisy timelines; SRE and product want deterministic, comparable baselines across hardware to make rollout decisions and to auto-generate human-readable one-line release notes for dashboards and email digests. What I changed: - registry/hw_baseline_sampler.py: new sampler that consumes recent perf telemetry and emits a compact baseline document (percentiles: p50/p90/p95/p99, median QPS, sample_count, sample_window) keyed by hardware flavor and model alias. The sampler is intentionally sampling-first (no heavy aggregation) and stores JSON-L snapshots in registry bucket. - registry/release_blurbs/templates.yaml: a small templating registry of presets (latency-first, throughput-first, regression-alert) with placeholders for delta percent and baseline anchors. - cli/generate_blurb.py: CLI helper used by release automation to synthesize micro-changelogs. Includes safety checks and a dry-run mode. - tests/test_hw_sampler.py: unit coverage for the sampler and template rendering. - docs/onboarding/hw-profiles.md: onboarding guide describing hardware classes, selection heuristics, and recommended sampling windows. - examples/sample_hw_profile.json: sample profile used by infra and partners. - ci/pipelines/model-registry.yml: CI matrix addition to test sampler across linux/x86 and aarch64 runners. Design notes: - Hardware classes are defined by a short canonical tag (e.g., a100-40gb, h100-80gb, g5-48gb, arm-a72). The sampler groups telemetry by tag and uses a rolling-window reservoir to avoid spikes. - Percentile choices reflect operational priorities: p90/p95 catch tail-latency regressions; p99 triggers alerts in our alerting playbooks. - Release blurbs are intentionally terse (one or two lines) with a single numeric delta and a link to the detailed profile for engineers. Rollout plan: - Merge to main; release automation will use the CLI in dry-run for one week to validate generated blurbs. - After validation enable the blurb autopublish flag for non-critical model updates (can be opted out in model metadata). Testing & validation: - Unit tests added and passing. - Local smoke runs on sandbox telemetry show stable baselines across A100/H100 with expected percentile differences. - CI now runs aarch64 matrix to catch platform-specific issues. Risks & mitigations: - Incorrect hardware tagging could produce misleading baselines: sampler now emits a warn metric when tag coverage < 20% and falls back to cohort baseline. - Template wording may be interpreted as authoritative: blurbs include a 'summary' prefix and a link back to the full profile so reviewers can always see raw numbers. Related work: ENG-4123 requested hardware-focused baselines; PM-217 asked for one-line release notes for model rollouts. This PR integrates with the existing model-profile schema and is compatible with the release-note assembler. Notes: kept implementation small and easily toggled by feature flag to limit blast radius.
release_notes: Adds a hardware-aware baseline sampler and a small registry of release-blurb templates; enables concise micro-changelogs for model releases. Default behavior is behind a feature flag; no breaking changes.
